questions.question: In an isobaric process, $n = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$ of a monatomic ideal gas is heated from $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ to $T_2 = 500\ \mathrm{K}$ at constant pressure $P = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Find: (a) the work done by the gas, (b) $\Delta U$, (c) the heat absorbed $Q$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Work in isobaric process: $W = P\Delta V = nR\Delta T$

$W = 2 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 3324\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** $\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 4986\ \mathrm{J}$

**(c)** $Q = \Delta U + W = 4986 + 3324 = 8310\ \mathrm{J}$

Alternatively: $Q = nC_P\Delta T = n\cdot\dfrac{5}{2}R\cdot\Delta T = 2 \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 200 = 8310\ \mathrm{J}$ ✓

questions.question: In an isobaric process, an ideal gas does $W = 600\ \mathrm{J}$ of work. The internal energy increases by $\Delta U = 900\ \mathrm{J}$. Find: (a) the heat absorbed by the gas, (b) how $Q$ is distributed.
questions.answer:
**(a)** First Law: $Q = \Delta U + W = 900 + 600 = 1500\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** Of the $1500\ \mathrm{J}$ of heat absorbed:
- $900\ \mathrm{J}$ (60%) increases the internal energy (raises the temperature)
- $600\ \mathrm{J}$ (40%) is converted to mechanical work done by the expanding gas

questions.question: A gas expands isobarically at $P = 2.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ from $V_1 = 3.0\ \mathrm{L}$ to $V_2 = 8.0\ \mathrm{L}$. Find the work done by the gas.
For a monatomic ideal gas, show that in an isobaric process the heat added is split as: $\tfrac{3}{5}$ goes to internal energy and $\tfrac{2}{5}$ goes to work.
questions.answer:
In an isobaric process:

$Q = nC_P\Delta T = n\cdot\dfrac{5}{2}R\cdot\Delta T$

$\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T = n\cdot\dfrac{3}{2}R\cdot\Delta T$

$W = nR\Delta T$

Fractions:

$\dfrac{\Delta U}{Q} = \dfrac{\frac{3}{2}R}{\frac{5}{2}R} = \dfrac{3}{5}$ ✓

$\dfrac{W}{Q} = \dfrac{R}{\frac{5}{2}R} = \dfrac{2}{5}$ ✓

$\dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5} = 1$ ✓

questions.question: During an isobaric cooling, $n = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas releases $Q = -1500\ \mathrm{J}$ of heat. Find: (a) the temperature change, (b) the work done by the gas.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $Q = nC_P\Delta T = n \cdot \dfrac{5}{2}R \cdot \Delta T$

$\Delta T = \dfrac{2Q}{5nR} = \dfrac{2(-1500)}{5 \times 1 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{-3000}{41.55} \approx -72.2\ \mathrm{K}$

Temperature decreases by $72.2\ \mathrm{K}$.

**(b)** $W = nR\Delta T = 1 \times 8.31 \times (-72.2) \approx -600\ \mathrm{J}$

Negative work: the environment does work **on** the gas as it contracts.

questions.question: A monatomic ideal gas expands isobarically from state A ($T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, $V = 2\ \mathrm{L}$) to state B ($T = 600\ \mathrm{K}$, $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$). Find: (a) the pressure, (b) the number of moles, (c) $\Delta U$, $W$, and $Q$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** From Charles's law ($V/T = $ const): $\dfrac{V_A}{T_A} = \dfrac{2}{300} = \dfrac{4}{600}$ ✓. Pressure from PV = nRT.

**(b)** At state A: $n = \dfrac{P V_A}{R T_A}$. From the isobaric law: $\dfrac{V_B}{T_B} = \dfrac{V_A}{T_A}$, so $P$ is unchanged. Assume $P = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$:

$n = \dfrac{1.0\times10^5 \times 2\times10^{-3}}{8.31 \times 300} = \dfrac{200}{2493} \approx 0.0803\ \mathrm{mol}$

**(c)** $\Delta T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 0.0803 \times 8.31 \times 300 \approx 300\ \mathrm{J}$

$W = nR\Delta T = 0.0803 \times 8.31 \times 300 \approx 200\ \mathrm{J}$

$Q = \Delta U + W = 500\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: Why is more heat required to raise the temperature of an ideal gas by $\Delta T$ at constant pressure than at constant volume? Explain using $C_P > C_V$.
questions.answer:
At **constant volume**: all added heat goes into increasing internal energy (raising temperature).

$Q_V = nC_V\Delta T$

At **constant pressure**: the gas expands as it is heated. Some of the added heat is "used up" doing expansion work against the constant external pressure:

$Q_P = nC_P\Delta T = n(C_V + R)\Delta T = nC_V\Delta T + nR\Delta T$

The extra $nR\Delta T$ is the work done by the gas during expansion.

Therefore $C_P = C_V + R > C_V$: you must supply extra heat at constant pressure to achieve the same temperature rise, because some heat leaves the system as work.

questions.question: A gas is heated isobarically and its volume increases from $V_1 = 5\ \mathrm{L}$ to $V_2 = 9\ \mathrm{L}$. During this process $\Delta U = 1200\ \mathrm{J}$. Find: (a) the pressure, (b) the heat added.
questions.answer:
**(a)** The work done:

$W = P\Delta V = P(V_2 - V_1) = P \times 4\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

For a monatomic ideal gas, $W = \frac{2}{3}\Delta U$:

$W = \frac{2}{3} \times 1200 = 800\ \mathrm{J}$

$P = \dfrac{W}{\Delta V} = \dfrac{800}{4\times10^{-3}} = 2.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**(b)** $Q = \Delta U + W = 1200 + 800 = 2000\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: For a diatomic ideal gas (5 degrees of freedom), $C_V = \frac{5}{2}R$ and $C_P = \frac{7}{2}R$. Compare the heat needed to raise $n = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ by $\Delta T = 100\ \mathrm{K}$: (a) at constant volume, (b) at constant pressure.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $Q_V = nC_V\Delta T = 1 \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 100 = 2077.5\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** $Q_P = nC_P\Delta T = 1 \times \dfrac{7}{2} \times 8.31 \times 100 = 2908.5\ \mathrm{J}$

Difference: $Q_P - Q_V = nR\Delta T = 831\ \mathrm{J}$ = the work done by the gas in the isobaric case.

questions.question: A piston–cylinder device contains $n = 3\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas. The gas is heated at constant pressure from $T_1 = 250\ \mathrm{K}$ until the volume doubles. Find: (a) the final temperature, (b) $Q$, $W$, $\Delta U$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Isobaric: $V \propto T$. If volume doubles, temperature doubles:

$T_2 = 2T_1 = 500\ \mathrm{K}$, so $\Delta T = 250\ \mathrm{K}$

**(b)** $W = nR\Delta T = 3 \times 8.31 \times 250 = 6232.5\ \mathrm{J}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 6232.5 = 9348.75\ \mathrm{J}$ (or $= \frac{3}{2} \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 250$)

$Q = \Delta U + W = 9348.75 + 6232.5 = 15{,}581.25\ \mathrm{J} \approx 15.6\ \mathrm{kJ}$
